chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about game that was shot in the open country (al-Hill) and then brought into the Sanctuary (al-Haram) while it was still alive. He said: 'If it is brought into the Sanctuary while it is alive, its meat becomes prohibited and its keeping becomes prohibited.'
And he said: 'Do not buy it in the Sanctuary unless it is slaughtered, having been slaughtered in the open country and then brought into the Sanctuary; there is no harm with it.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca), where hunting is prohibited
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open country or non-sanctuary area where hunting is permitted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on game brought into the Haram while still alive versus slaughtered in the Hill?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the state of the animal and the location of its slaughter regarding the sanctity of the Haram. It establishes that bringing game in alive invalidates its permissibility due to the violation of the sanctuary's peace, whereas pre-slaughter in the open country preserves its status as lawful food. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical integrity of the sacrifice relative to the sacred boundaries.
